horizon_driver: biennial House majority at stake in the Nov 3 2026 midterms; presidential term to Jan 2029; donor-cycle and security-establishment horizons run much longer than the electoral one, which is the source of the faction split the Cartographer flags

capabilities.description: e.g. license carve-outs / revenue-share export deals, trade-surcharge negotiations, swap-line-adjacent accommodations
e.g. tariff/export-control tightening, sanctions expansion, security-guarantee signaling; demonstrated reversible in practice (IEEPA tariffs unwound within days of the Feb 2026 SCOTUS ruling)

constraints.source: Supreme Court, Learning Resources Inc. v. Trump / V.O.S. Selections v. United States, 6-3, Feb 20 2026: IEEPA does not authorize tariffs; >$160bn collected ruled unlawful
constraints.breaks_under: administration pivots same-day to alternate statutory authority (Section 122 of the Trade Act of 1974, 10% global surcharge proclaimed Feb 20 2026) — the constraint bites on IEEPA specifically, not on the policy goal, so treat as a legal-venue constraint, not a substantive one

constraints.source: Trump v. Cook, SCOTUS 5-4, June 29 2026: blocked the Aug 2025 attempted for-cause removal of Governor Lisa Cook for lack of statutory procedural protections
constraints.breaks_under: a properly noticed, documented for-cause process — the Court explicitly left this open ('punted on several key questions'), so the constraint is real but narrow

constraints.source: unbroken full-faith-and-credit norm; every debt-ceiling standoff (including 2023, 2025) has resolved before default; Treasury market centrality to global collateral system
constraints.breaks_under: no historical instance; treat as near-physics constraint, revisit only if a debt-ceiling standoff runs past X-date with no legislative vehicle available

constraints.source: burden-shifting rhetoric (2025-2026) toward European and allied capitals coexists with continued troop presence, continued arms transfers, and continued extended-deterrence statements
constraints.breaks_under: sustained European defense spending below political patience threshold, or a crisis where non-intervention becomes politically cheaper than intervention

stated_vs_revealed.stated: Export-control doctrine toward China semiconductors is 'small yard, high fence' — a fixed national-security containment line, not a bargaining chip.
stated_vs_revealed.revealed: In Aug 2025 the administration approved Nvidia H20 export licenses to China conditioned on a 15% revenue cut to the US Treasury; by Dec 2025-Jan 2026 this was expanded to a 25% levy on Nvidia H200 and equivalent AMD/Intel parts, formalized by proclamation Jan 14 2026, with chips routed through the US for third-party testing before re-export.
stated_vs_revealed.delta: The 'containment' line is priced, not fixed — a revenue-extraction mechanism, not a security barrier. Legal scholars note ECRA bars license 'fees,' meaning the arrangement's durability is itself contested.

stated_vs_revealed.stated: Fed independence is respected as an institutional norm ('let the Fed do its job').
stated_vs_revealed.revealed: In Aug 2025 the President attempted the first-ever removal of a sitting Fed Governor (Lisa Cook), the first attempted Governor firing in the Fed's 111-year history; blocked 5-4 by the Supreme Court in June 2026, but only on narrow due-process grounds, with the Court explicitly leaving open whether a compliant for-cause process would succeed.
stated_vs_revealed.delta: Independence held this round on a procedural technicality, not a substantive bright line — the norm is now known to be contestable at the personnel layer.

stated_vs_revealed.stated: 'Liberation Day'/IEEPA tariffs represent a durable strategic realignment of trade policy, justified by a declared national emergency.
stated_vs_revealed.revealed: Struck down 6-3 by the Supreme Court Feb 20 2026 as exceeding IEEPA authority; the administration terminated IEEPA tariffs within days and pivoted the same day to a 10% global surcharge under Section 122 of the Trade Act of 1974 — a different, time-limited legal basis.
stated_vs_revealed.delta: The policy goal (broad tariff leverage) is durable; the legal vehicle is opportunistic and was swapped out overnight with no change in substantive posture, showing doctrine follows the goal rather than constrains it.

stated_vs_revealed.stated: Restore fiscal responsibility / reduce the federal deficit.
stated_vs_revealed.revealed: The One Big Beautiful Bill Act (signed July 2025) is projected by CBO to add ~$3.0-3.4tn to the deficit over 2025-2034 including debt-service costs; CBO's Feb 2026 outlook raised the FY2026 deficit projection to ~$2.1tn (~5.8% of GDP), driven by the bill, higher tariffs, and lower immigration.
stated_vs_revealed.delta: Consistent, large gap between stated restraint and enacted fiscal expansion — this is the least credible domain for ST_US.

tripwires.if: core PCE re-accelerates above ~3% while unemployment also rises within ~6 months of the Nov 2026 midterms
tripwires.then: White House intensifies public and legal pressure on the Fed for cuts (as with the Aug 2025 Cook removal attempt and the Miran appointment), regardless of the narrow SCOTUS ruling

ST_US moves to maximum-severity semiconductor export controls on China, overriding any standing revenue-share licensing arrangements (H20/H200-style deals) — the 'chip diplomacy' regime is a peacetime-only equilibrium

tripwires.if: a future for-cause Fed Board removal attempt follows the due-process procedure the Court specified in Trump v. Cook
tripwires.then: expect it to succeed where the 2025 Cook attempt failed — the independence norm is now a checklist, not a wall

what_would_change_my_mind: Direct polling/roll-call evidence that the four cartographer-flagged factions (restrainers, primacists, industrial-policy left, fiscal hawks) vote as distinct blocs on a specific bill or nomination — I found no such factional voting data and modeled ST_US as unitary; if legitimacy falls further and a real faction split shows up in roll calls, this dossier should be split into 2+ actors per the Cartographer's own note. Also watch for the outcome of any second Fed-governor removal attempt under the Trump v. Cook standard, which would sharply change the independence-credibility score.
